goals: mechanistic: quantify how soil clay content controls the partitioning of infiltrated/precipitated water between surface runoff and deep drainage (recharge), holding climate/vegetation/topography fixed
key_processes: soil water retention and saturated hydraulic conductivity as functions of texture
evapotranspiration partitioning (fixed vegetation, but responds to soil moisture)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM directly simulates water partitioning (QOVER, QDRAI/recharge, ET, per-layer soil moisture) and lets soil texture be set per column; a controlled clay sweep with one fixed forcing isolates the texture mechanism.

answerable: clay-content control on surface-runoff vs deep-drainage partitioning under fixed forcing
nonlinearity of the partitioning response across the 5-55% clay range
associated shifts in root-zone soil moisture and ET

sampling_strategy.approach: controlled / not spatial — single-factor level sweep
sampling_strategy.n_justification: One controlled factor with a strongly nonlinear expected response (Ks and water-retention curves vary sharply with texture). 6 evenly spaced levels across 5-55% resolve both the trend and its curvature while keeping the sweep minimal; fewer risks aliasing the nonlinearity, more adds cost without new information.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: controlled / not spatial — each level is a synthetic column identical except for clay fraction; all other soil, forcing, vegetation, and topographic properties held fixed.
sampling_strategy.replication: none — deterministic controlled experiment, no spatial variance to average over

sampling_plan.reason: high-Ks endmember; expected recharge-dominated partitioning, low surface runoff
loamy-sand/sandy-loam range; early part of the transition curve
loam range; mid-transition where partitioning shifts most rapidly
clay-loam range; increasing runoff fraction, declining recharge
clay range; low-Ks behavior, runoff-dominated regime onset
low-Ks endmember; expected runoff-dominated, recharge-suppressed partitioning

validation_design.observation_source: physical expectation / pedotransfer literature (no in-domain observations in this conceptual design)
validation_design.comparison: analog — compare simulated monotonic decline in recharge fraction with clay against theoretical Ks-texture and water-retention expectations
validation_design.metric: qualitative monotonicity + slope of partitioning-vs-clay response; internal consistency of water budget closure

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: single fixed representative NLDAS-2 forcing window with multi-year spin-up; synthetic uniform soil column; only clay fraction varied

requires_capabilities.why: recharge and deep drainage are slow states; without ~5+ spin-up years each column cold-starts at the default ~8.8 m water table and early recharge reads ~0 while storage fills
requires_capabilities.blocks: meaningful, non-artifact recharge/drainage partitioning — the primary target

requires_capabilities.capability: synthetic/parametric soil specification (set clay fraction directly, with a rule for the complementary sand/silt split and other hydraulic properties held fixed)
requires_capabilities.why: the experiment requires controlled uniform soils that vary ONLY in clay content rather than SSURGO-sampled real soils
requires_capabilities.blocks: clean isolation of the clay effect

requires_capabilities.capability: recharge/drainage diagnostic output (QDRAI, QRECHARGE, QOVER) written to history
requires_capabilities.why: partitioning ratio is the response variable and must be in the output stream

assumptions: The complementary (non-clay) soil fraction is assigned by a fixed rule (e.g. constant silt:sand ratio) so that only clay varies; the configurator must define this.
A single representative forcing window within 1980-2018 is chosen and held identical across all 6 levels; results are conditional on that climate.
Vegetation, organic matter, soil depth/layering, and slope are held fixed at a single representative configuration.
Uniform-texture soil column (no vertical texture layering) unless otherwise specified.
Partitioning is evaluated on post-spin-up years only, averaged to annual/seasonal means.
open_questions: Which representative forcing window/climate should anchor the experiment (humid vs semi-arid strongly changes the runoff/recharge balance)?
Should the complementary fraction be held as constant silt:sand, or should sand be the sole filler (this changes Ks trajectory)?
Is a fixed water-table lower boundary desired, or free drainage, for the recharge definition?
Preferred spin-up length / acceptable drift tolerance before analysis years?
